SpecialtyRx reports up to 40% higher per-station medication throughput with tSort

Robotic sortation follows pharmacist finalization, automating scan-and-route work for prescriptions bound for care facilities.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗19 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

Robots in medication fulfillment

SpecialtyRx has disclosed its use of Tompkins Robotics’ tSort for prescriptions destined for long-term care facilities. The provider processes more than 55,000 prescriptions daily. Robots handle a fulfillment stage after a pharmacist has finalized a prescription; they do not replace prescribing decisions or pharmacist review.

Reading the station-level comparison

Technicians previously scanned and sorted prescriptions individually, with an approximate baseline of 1,000 prescriptions per hour. The company reports a current tSort maximum of 1,400 per hour, an increase of up to 40% per station. That maximum is not a network-wide average, and the release provides no independent medication-error evaluation.

Modular expansion within existing space

tSort combines mobile robots with modular sorting infrastructure, allowing additional robots and destinations without new construction. It complements investments in dispensing, packaging and digital delivery verification. Operational value depends on consistent routing and handling peak volumes, not simply the speed of an individual robot.
